findings.text: The fragment states 'the replay now passes a claim that always permits', which the delivered head no longer does: reckon/evidence at a874e779 passes NO_LIFT_CLAIM (reckon/crew/ticker.py:2984), and the same fragment contradicts itself forty lines later, so the node's own record misdescribes the shipped behaviour it was written to document.

The arms table names cd8299c02e as the after arm's revision while the manifest's after_suite and the head-arm log's '# revision:' header both name a874e779576b, so a reader comparing the revision a review read against the commits being promoted is given an sha no arm was run at and the evidence cannot be reconciled with its own log.

the assertion compares the drawn row's lift_id against the literal 'reset-claude-sub-20261115T183000Z' that the test's own _write_reset default supplied to the code under test, so it holds whatever the claim logic does; the same shape appears at :178. The count assertions at :139, :154-156 and :177 carry the real guard, which the mutation log shows firing.

PaneRowPath.__init__ still annotates lift_claim as Callable[[str, str], bool] | None while RowPolicy accepts and is handed _NoLiftClaim (ticker.py:1729, :1820), and replay_row_policy passes the sentinel through this very signature at :2984, so the single sentinel crosses an annotation that says it cannot and a future type check would reject the delivered call.

_pane_lift_claim returns no claim when the path names no session, so a follower armed without --session (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:3276 makes --session optional) now draws every limit reset on its own memory where the base claim key mapped it to the shared 'pane' directory (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:952), leaving exactly the one-row-per-pane defect reachable for a session-less pane served by more than one follower; the run discloses this narrowing under evidence_inputs but no test covers it either way.
